title: Graceful fallback when offline file:// missing -> re-resolve to stream
description: Today dangling file:// fails playback with no recovery.
design:
DEPENDS ON Lunara-uww.3.1 (which folds in 3.2). Do this AFTER the 3.1/3.2 resolver PR lands — it builds directly on PlaybackURLResolving.

WHAT 3.1 ALREADY SOLVES (do not re-implement)
OfflineStore.localFileURL(forTrackID:) (Lunara/Library/Offline/OfflineStore.swift:13-31) already calls FileManager.fileExists; if the offline file is missing on disk it deletes the stale OfflineTrackRecord row and returns nil. The 3.1 resolver consults this, so a registered-but-deleted offline file already falls through to a fresh stream URL AT RESOLVE TIME. The "dangling file:// at build/resolve time" case is therefore handled by 3.1.

REMAINING GAP THIS BEAD CLOSES (reactive failures fileExists cannot catch)
Engine load can still fail AFTER a URL is resolved:
  (a) offline file exists on disk but is corrupt/truncated/unreadable -> AVAudioPlayer load throws;
  (b) file deleted in the race window between resolve and engine.load;
  (c) the resolved stream URL itself fails to load (token edge, transient).
In all three, CrossfadeEngine.play -> activeSlot.load throws (CrossfadeEngine.swift:61-67) -> transitionToError sets playbackState=.error(message) (406-412). QueueManager.handleEngineStateChange (QueueManager.swift:375-403) only reacts to .idle (advance) and trackID sync — it IGNORES .error. Result: playback dead-ends with no recovery. That is this bug.

IMPORTANT ENGINE QUIRK: on a failed play(), CrossfadeEngine sets currentTrackID only on success (line 76), and transitionToError does NOT reset it. So engine.currentTrackID is unreliable for identifying which item failed. Recovery MUST key off QueueManager.currentItem (its own currentIndex), not engine.currentTrackID.

DESIGN

1) Resolver gains an offline-skip mode — Lunara/Music/Queue/PlaybackURLResolver.swift (created in 3.1)
   Change signature to: func resolvePlaybackURL(for item: QueueItem, allowOffline: Bool) async throws -> URL.
   allowOffline=true (default call site behavior): current 3.1 logic (offline-then-stream).
   allowOffline=false: SKIP the offline branch entirely, return try await library.streamURL(forKey: item.streamKey). Needed so the retry doesn't just re-pick the same bad offline file (case (a), where fileExists still passes).
   Update the 3.1 call sites in QueueManager.playCurrentItem / prepareNextTrackIfNeeded to pass allowOffline: true.

2) QueueManager reactive recovery — Lunara/Music/Queue/QueueManager.swift
   Add state: private var streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID: String? (guards against infinite retry loops).
   In handleEngineStateChange, add an .error branch (before/after the existing .idle check): if engine.playbackState.hasError, let item = currentItem, and streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID != item.trackID -> set streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID = item.trackID and call a new recoverCurrentItemViaStream(). If streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID == item.trackID (stream retry ALSO failed) -> stop retrying: set lastError = .playbackFailed/streamFailed and leave the error surfaced (do NOT loop, do NOT silently advance).
   recoverCurrentItemViaStream(): re-resolve currentItem with allowOffline:false, then engine.play(url: streamURL, trackID:), preserving position via pendingSeekAfterNextPlay = lastPersistedElapsed (so a mid-track failure resumes near where it died). Mirror the Task/MainActor + signalBuffering pattern already in playCurrentItem (since a stream URL is remote -> runs through TrackCache path). On resolver throw here, set lastError and stop.
   Clear streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID whenever a DIFFERENT track starts successfully (e.g. in syncCurrentIndexToEngineTrack and advanceAndPlayNextIfPossible / at the top of a successful playCurrentItem) so each track gets one fresh recovery attempt.

3) Consider routing the recovery through playCurrentItem with an internal "forceStream" flag instead of a separate method, to avoid duplicating the TrackCache/seek/persist block. Implementer's choice; keep it DRY.

EDGE CASES / NOTES
- Loop guard is essential: offline-corrupt -> error -> stream retry -> stream also errors must terminate, not ping-pong.
- handleEngineStateChange currently early-returns during manualNavigationTargetTrackID suppression (378-384); make sure the .error branch isn't swallowed when a manual nav target is set and the target track fails to load — likely want recovery to still fire for the manual target.
- prepareNext (crossfade next-track) dead-file failures are logged-and-skipped today (CrossfadeEngine.swift:184-194); leaving next-track recovery OUT OF SCOPE is acceptable — the failed next track will just re-resolve when it becomes current. Note this explicitly; do not gold-plate.

TESTING (Swift Testing; iPhone 17 Pro OS:26.2). Failing first, show red.
   - PlaybackURLResolver: allowOffline:false returns a stream URL even when an offline file IS present for the trackID.
   - QueueManager: engine enters .error while playing current item -> QueueManager re-resolves with allowOffline:false and calls engine.play with the stream URL (use a mock engine that records play() calls + a mock resolver).
   - QueueManager: stream retry ALSO errors -> no second re-resolve (loop guard holds), lastError is set.
   - QueueManager: streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID resets when a different track begins (so a later failure on another track still recovers).
   - QueueManager: recovery preserves position (pendingSeekAfterNextPlay == lastPersistedElapsed at retry).
acceptance_criteria:
- When the engine fails to load the current item (corrupt offline file, file deleted post-resolve, or stream load failure), QueueManager automatically re-resolves forcing a stream and retries playback once.
- The retry does NOT reuse the failed offline file (resolver allowOffline:false path).
- If the stream retry also fails, playback stops with a surfaced lastError and does NOT loop infinitely.
- Recovery keys off QueueManager.currentItem, not engine.currentTrackID.
- Each distinct track gets exactly one recovery attempt (guard resets on new track).
- Mid-track failures resume near the prior playback position.
- prepareNext/crossfade next-track failures remain logged-and-skipped (explicitly out of scope).
- Full test suite green on iPhone 17 Pro OS:26.2.
notes: Implemented reactive stream recovery (#60 lazy-resolver seam). Resolver gained allowOffline:; QueueManager .error branch (top of handleEngineStateChange, above manual-nav guard) re-resolves forcing stream once per track, guarded by streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID + lastPlayedURLWasFile, resumes via pendingSeekAfterNextPlay=lastPersistedElapsed. Also: failed play now skips persist/prepareNext (was clobbering lastError via persist-success clear). Crossfade-advanced failures stay out of scope (lastPlayedURLWasFile reset in syncCurrentIndexToEngineTrack). 9 new tests (8 QueueManager + 1 resolver). Full suite green on iPhone 17 Pro OS 26.4.1. Pending: commit + push.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #61 (squash-merged to main). Reactive stream recovery: resolver allowOffline, QueueManager .error branch with per-track guard, position-preserving single retry. 9 tests, full suite green.

title: Queue persists stable track IDs, not resolved URLs
description: QueueManager.swift:296 bakes URLs at build time; breaks after download/delete.
design:
SCOPE: This bead is being executed TOGETHER WITH Lunara-uww.3.2 (lazy URL resolution). They are inseparable — the moment QueueItem stops carrying a baked URL, the play path has nothing to play, which is exactly what 3.2 fills in. One PR closes both. Decisions confirmed with maintainer 2026-06-05: (1) combine 3.1+3.2; (2) store stable Plex stream key in QueueItem (no Track re-fetch at play time).

ROOT CAUSE
QueueItem carries `url: URL` (Lunara/Music/Queue/QueueManagerProtocol.swift:6). It is resolved once at queue-build time in AppRouter.resolveQueueItemsConcurrently / queueItem(for:) (Lunara/Router/AppRouter.swift:266-331) and that resolved URL is persisted in QueueSnapshot. QueueManager.playCurrentItem (QueueManager.swift:174-213) and prepareNextTrackIfNeeded (227-266) read currentItem.url directly. Consequences after enqueue: a track downloaded later keeps replaying the remote stream; a deleted offline file replays a dead file:// URL; a persisted stream URL carries an expired X-Plex-Token across launches.

streamURL(forTrack:) (Lunara/Library/API/PlexAPIClient.swift:134-147) only uses track.key + a fresh token. So track.key is the single stable input needed to rebuild a stream URL at play time — store it, don't re-fetch the Track.

DESIGN

1) Model — Lunara/Music/Queue/QueueManagerProtocol.swift
   QueueItem: replace `let url: URL` with `let streamKey: String` (= Plex track.key). Keep trackID (plexID), albumID, trackNumber. Update init. Persisted QueueSnapshot now holds stable identifiers only. NOTE: this changes the on-disk Codable shape — old persisted queues will fail to decode. FileQueueStatePersistence.load() already catches decode errors and QueueManager.restorePersistedQueue handles a throw by clearing to empty (QueueManager.swift:316-322), so a one-time queue reset on upgrade is acceptable. Confirm no migration is wanted (default: none).

2) Stream-URL-from-key primitive
   - Lunara/Library/API/PlexAPIClient.swift: add `func streamURL(forKey key: String) async throws -> URL` containing the components/token build currently in streamURL(forTrack:); make streamURL(forTrack:) call streamURL(forKey: track.key).
   - Lunara/Library/Repo/LibraryRepoProtocol.swift + LibraryRepo.swift: surface `streamURL(forKey:)` through the repo protocol (delegates to remote), mirroring the existing streamURL(for:) plumbing (LibraryRepo.swift:215-218, LibraryRepoProtocol.swift:86/226).

3) Resolver (new) — Lunara/Music/Queue/PlaybackURLResolver.swift
   protocol PlaybackURLResolving: Sendable { func resolvePlaybackURL(for item: QueueItem) async throws -> URL }
   Concrete impl holds offlineStore (OfflineStoreProtocol?) + library (LibraryRepoProtocol). Logic: if let offlineStore, let localURL = try await offlineStore.localFileURL(forTrackID: item.trackID) { return localURL } else { return try await library.streamURL(forKey: item.streamKey) }. This is AppRouter.resolveURL (AppRouter.swift:24-30) re-homed to operate on a QueueItem instead of a Track.

4) QueueManager — Lunara/Music/Queue/QueueManager.swift
   Add optional `resolver: PlaybackURLResolving?` (same optional-injection pattern as trackCache/loudnessProvider, init lines 36-48). In playCurrentItem (171-214): resolve the URL via resolver at play time, THEN keep the existing isFileURL-vs-TrackCache branch on the resolved URL (file/local -> engine.play directly; remote -> signalBuffering + trackCache.prepare). Wrap in the existing Task; on resolver throw, set lastError and bail (do NOT play a stale URL). prepareNextTrackIfNeeded (216-273): resolve nextItem URL the same way before the isFileURL branch. If resolver is nil (tests that don't inject one), preserve current behavior is impossible since url is gone — tests must inject a resolver mock (see tests).

5) Wiring — Lunara/App/AppCoordinator.swift
   offlineStore is currently built AFTER queueManager (104-117). Reorder: build offlineStore + offlineDirectory first, then construct the resolver (offlineStore + libraryRepo), then pass resolver into QueueManager(...). AppRouter still receives offlineStore as today (122).

6) Builders — Lunara/Router/AppRouter.swift
   Stop resolving URLs at build time. resolveQueueItemsConcurrently (266-291) and queueItem(for:) (320-331) emit QueueItem(trackID: track.plexID, streamKey: track.key, albumID: track.albumID, trackNumber: track.trackNumber). Delete resolveURL (24-30) and the per-item URL resolution inside the task group. Builders no longer need offlineStore for URL purposes (verify no other use before removing).

TESTING (Swift Testing; iPhone 17 Pro OS:26.2). Write failing first, show red.
   - QueueStatePersistenceTests: round-trip stores/restores streamKey, no url field present. Update existing QueueItem(...url:...) literals (lines ~23,24,51).
   - QueueManagerTests: inject a PlaybackURLResolving mock. (a) playCurrentItem calls resolver and plays the resolved URL; (b) download-after-enqueue: resolver returns file:// the second time -> engine plays local; (c) resolver throw -> lastError set, engine NOT asked to play a stale URL. Update all QueueItem(...url:...) literals (lines 186-209+ and elsewhere).
   - NowPlayingScreenViewModelTests, AppRouterTests, AppCoordinatorTests: update QueueItem constructions to streamKey.
   - AppRouterTests: builders emit streamKey from track.key and no longer call streamURL at build time.

OUT OF SCOPE (separate beads): 3.4 graceful fallback when offline file:// missing -> re-resolve to stream (resolver makes this trivial later); 3.6 re-resolve queue on download complete/remove; 3.5 unify OfflineStore+TrackCache.
acceptance_criteria:
- QueueItem no longer has a `url` field; carries trackID + streamKey + albumID + trackNumber.
- Persisted QueueSnapshot contains no resolved URLs (stable IDs only); round-trip test passes.
- URL is resolved at PLAY time via PlaybackURLResolving: offline file if present, else fresh stream URL from streamKey.
- Track downloaded AFTER enqueue plays the local file on next play without rebuilding the queue (test).
- Resolver failure sets lastError and does not play a stale URL (test).
- LibraryRepoProtocol exposes streamURL(forKey:); streamURL(forTrack:) delegates to it.
- AppRouter builders no longer resolve URLs at build time.
- Full test suite green on iPhone 17 Pro OS:26.2.
notes: Folds in Lunara-uww.3.2 (close both together). Maintainer decisions 2026-06-05: combine 3.1+3.2; store streamKey in QueueItem (no Track re-fetch). Open micro-decision left to implementer: no on-disk migration for old persisted queues (one-time reset on upgrade is acceptable since restore already clears on decode error).
close_reason: Already shipped in commit bd2021b (#60): QueueItem carries streamKey, PlaybackURLResolver resolves lazily at play time, wired in AppCoordinator. Beads were stale/open.

title: Now Playing UI doesn't update when track auto-advances at end-of-track
description:
REPRO: Artist page (Mumford & Sons) -> Shuffle -> Now Playing screen opens, plays 'Little Lion Man' (correct). When the track ENDS, audio advances to the next track (audible, correct) BUT the Now Playing UI does NOT update: still shows old track title + same waveform/visualizer. The animated playhead resets to start (white) but it's the SAME waveform/metadata as the previous track, not the new one.

SYMPTOMS:
- Engine + audio advance correctly; only the Now Playing VIEW is stale.
- Playhead resets but waveform/title do not refresh to the new track.
- Also observed: UI was 'extremely laggy / not buttery smooth' during playback (separate perf concern; may be debug build or main-thread work — note but verify).

LIKELY AREA (engine auto-advance -> QueueManager sync -> NowPlaying VM observation):
- CrossfadeEngine.handleTrackEnded() swaps slots, plays next, sets currentTrackID = new track (Lunara/Music/Engine/CrossfadeEngine.swift ~343).
- QueueManager.observeEngineState/handleEngineStateChange -> syncCurrentIndexToEngineTrack advances currentIndex only if items[currentIndex+1].trackID == engineTrackID (QueueManager.swift ~395/440).
- NowPlayingScreenViewModel: determine whether it observes queueManager.currentIndex/currentItem or a snapshot cache keyed by trackID; suspected the view isn't reacting to the advance, OR the snapshot for the new track is missing/stale so it falls back to the old one. Snapshot cache eviction lives ~NowPlayingScreenViewModel:270-291.

RESEARCH GOAL: pin whether the break is (a) QueueManager not advancing currentIndex on natural end-of-track, or (b) NowPlaying VM/view not reacting to the advance / snapshot selection stale. Then propose fix.

NOTE: Found while collecting telemetry (Lunara-w4v); telemetry log from the session will show the engine handleTrackEnded->play event with the new trackID, confirming the engine advanced. Not caused by telemetry (engine emit calls are additive). Likely pre-existing, surfaced by playing through a track end.

title: Playback memory telemetry log (measure phase for epic 2)

Settings 'Record playback diagnostics' toggle (default off) + 'Share Playback Log' ShareLink. Purpose: quantify real 1-slot vs 2-slot footprint and check for leaks across real listening sessions, to reassess whether 2.1/2.2 are real or already resolved by the AVAudioPlayer migration (#60). MemoryProbe + PlaybackTelemetry (GCD sampler, ioQueue file writes mirroring FileQueueStatePersistence, authoritative slot count from engine). No playback behavior change.
notes: Implemented. MemoryProbe (task_info phys_footprint + os_proc_available_memory). PlaybackTelemetry @MainActor recorder backed by thread-safe nonisolated TelemetryWriter (GCD 5s sampler fires in background; ioQueue file appends; single-backup rotation at 5MB; UserDefaults-persisted isEnabled). CrossfadeEngine optional emitter, authoritative slot count [slotA,slotB].filter{trackID != nil}.count, emits at play/pause/resume/seek/prepareNext/crossfadeBegin/crossfadeComplete/handleTrackEnded/skip/stop/error, guarded by isEnabled. scenePhase->recordScenePhase in LunaraApp. Settings Diagnostics section: toggle + ShareLink + Clear. 8 tests (MemoryProbe + PlaybackTelemetry). Full unit+UI suite green. Next: manual device session to collect data.

title: Paginate library grid queries (stop load-all)
description: LibraryGridViewModel.swift:217 queryAlbums(.all) loads entire library into RAM.
design: KEYSET (not OFFSET): ordering already has unique tiebreaker plexID; OFFSET is O(n)/page and dup/skips during background refresh. ADD to LibraryStoreProtocol: struct AlbumCursor{artistName,title,plexID} + func queryAlbums(filter:after:limit:). Keep existing queryAlbums(filter:) for search. In LibraryStore+AlbumQueryPlanner: when cursor!=nil append row-value predicate (albums.artistName,albums.title,albums.plexID) > (?,?,?) ANDed with filter; keep ORDER BY artistName,title,plexID ASC; append LIMIT ?. Forward through LibraryRepo(+Protocol); add default not-implemented impl on PlexAPIClient ext to compile. In LibraryGridViewModel add pageSize=50, hasMorePages, nextCursor, isLoadingNextPage guard; reloadCachedCatalog loads first page; add loadNextPageIfNeeded(currentItem:) (early-return unless !isSearchActive && hasMorePages && !loading && album within last ~10). +BackgroundRefresh resets to first page (cursor nil). In LibraryGridView ForEach(filteredAlbums) add .task{await viewModel.loadNextPageIfNeeded(currentItem:album)}. FILES: LibraryStoreProtocol.swift, LibraryStore+AlbumQueryPlanner.swift, LibraryRepoProtocol.swift, LibraryRepo.swift, LibraryGridViewModel.swift, LibraryGridViewModel+BackgroundRefresh.swift, LibraryGridView.swift. OUT_OF_SCOPE: no offline sync/replaceLibrary/incremental-sync/schema/migration/index changes; dont paginate search path; dont touch artist/collection/playlist grids; leave fetchAlbums(page:) offset path alone.
acceptance_criteria: queryAlbums gains a keyset page API returning <=pageSize rows for a cursor; store test proves bounded page + next page has no gaps/overlaps. LibraryGridViewModel initial load puts only 50 into albums when catalog>50. Scrolling near end appends next 50 via loadNextPageIfNeeded; stops when a short page returns (hasMorePages=false, no infinite loop). Search/filter path unchanged and existing search tests pass.
notes: Implemented keyset pagination. AlbumCursor(artistName,title,plexID) + queryAlbums(filter:after:limit:) threaded through LibraryStore(+planner row-value predicate + LIMIT), LibraryRepo, protocols; PlexAPIClient stub + test-only defaults in TestDefaults so the many mocks didn't each need updating. VM: pageSize 50, centralized replaceCatalog/appendNextPage/finishPage with catalogGeneration guard (background-refresh-mid-fetch safety) + synchronous isLoadingNextPage flag (re-entrancy) + O(1) triggerAlbumID. Background refresh preserves loaded depth (max(pageSize,count)); pull-to-refresh resets to page 1; search path untouched. Per-item .task in albumCard. 11 new tests (3 store + 8 VM incl boundary/empty/re-entrancy/refresh/search-clear). Full unit+UI suite green on iPhone 17 Pro OS 26.4.1. Pending: commit/push/PR.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #63 (squash-merged). Keyset album pagination: AlbumCursor + queryAlbums(filter:after:limit:), centralized VM paging with re-entrancy + generation guards, search untouched. 11 tests, full suite green.

title: Bound/evict artworkByAlbumID dictionary
description: LibraryGridViewModel.swift:39 grows unbounded with library size.
design: Bound the unbounded var artworkByAlbumID:[String:URL] (line ~39) with LRU while keeping it an @Observable stored property (SwiftUI still re-renders) and preserving thumbnailURL(for:) read API (line ~116, view line ~161). Add private var artworkLRU:[String] (recency, most-recent last) + static artworkCacheCapacity=300. New private func storeArtwork(_:for:) used in loadThumbnailIfNeeded success (line ~141): move id to end of artworkLRU, set dict, while count>capacity removeFirst() from both. In thumbnailURL(for:) on hit move id to end (mark used). Eviction must not touch pendingArtworkAlbumIDs. Consider making capacity an init param defaulted to 300 so tests can pass a small value (avoid 300 awaited resolutions). FILES: LibraryGridViewModel.swift (optional new +ArtworkCache.swift), tests LibraryGridViewModelTests.swift. OUT_OF_SCOPE: dont touch ArtworkPipeline/on-disk cache, loadThumbnailIfNeeded fetch flow, pending dedupe semantics, AsyncImage usage, or other VMs artwork dicts.
acceptance_criteria: artworkByAlbumID never exceeds fixed cap (300); test proves count<=cap after resolving >cap distinct albums. LRU: recently-requested IDs retained, oldest dropped (test). pendingArtworkAlbumIDs doesnt leak across eviction (returns to empty). Re-requesting an evicted album re-resolves and re-inserts; existing artwork tests pass.
notes: TESTS first (LibraryGridViewModelTests.swift) using waitForArtworkResolution helper: (1) resolve cap+5 distinct albums -> artworkByAlbumID.count<=capacity (inject small capacity for speed); (2) LRU: resolve cap+1, first id evicted (thumbnailURL nil), newest present; touch secondOldest then resolve one more -> touched survives, next-oldest evicted; (3) pending cleanup: after eviction storm no stuck pending (re-request issues fresh thumbnailRequests). DEPENDENCY: after 4.1 (paging makes dict track scrolled window; 4.2-first would be masked by load-all flooding).

title: Fix album palette double-decode
description: AlbumDetailViewModel.swift:200 decodes full image twice for palette extraction.
design: Replace full Data->UIImage(data:) feeding ArtworkPaletteExtractor (which redraws into 50x50, ArtworkPaletteExtractor.swift:23) with a single small downsample: if let url, let img=DownsamplingImageLoader.load(contentsOf:url,maxPixelSize:64){palette=ArtworkPaletteExtractor.extract(from:img)}. 64px ample for 50x50 sampling. If 1.3 already moved this off-main, keep inside same Task.detached and just swap sizing to 64. Set artworkURL=url before decode. FILES: edit AlbumDetailViewModel.swift (loadArtwork) only. OUT_OF_SCOPE: dont change ArtworkPaletteExtractor 50x50 sampling, the view display path, artworkURL semantics, or other VMs.
acceptance_criteria: AlbumDetailViewModel.loadArtwork (~200) decodes artwork at most once for palette (no second full UIImage(data:)). palette still non-.default for valid artwork. artworkURL still set for the view display path.
notes: TESTS first, extend AlbumDetailViewModelTests.swift: seed fetchFullSize -> temp 1024px image with distinctive dominant color; await loadIfNeeded; #expect palette != .default and artworkURL != nil. DEPENDENCY: after 1.1; conflicts with 1.3 on loadArtwork - sequence after 1.3 or fold together.
close_reason: Already implemented + tested in #60 (bd2021b): loadArtwork does a single DownsamplingImageLoader decode at 64px off-main via Task.detached, no second UIImage(data:). Covered by AlbumDetailViewModelTests.loadIfNeeded_resolvesPaletteFromArtwork (palette != .default, artworkURL set). Bead was stale/in_progress.
